intro_html: Poppy seed chicken is Southern potluck royalty: tender chicken folded into a rich, buttery cream sauce flecked with poppy seeds, baked over rice under a crunchy buttered cracker topping until bubbling. Pure comfort, zero pretension. Each serving brings 25 grams of protein for about $1.29, one of the cheapest dinners on our whole board.
cost_closing_html: About $1.29 a bowl for creamy Southern comfort that a meat-and-three cafe would plate for $12. The entire 14-serving batch costs about what two of those plates would.
shop_smart: The whole batch rang up around $18.02, and chicken was only $5.06 of it. When a casserole this rich comes in under $19 total, you double the recipe and thank the freezer later.
This version builds its cream sauce from scratch with butter, flour, and broth instead of canned soup. It costs less than the cans and you can pronounce everything in it.
The signature cracker topping costs about 58 cents from a store-brand box of butter crackers, and the rest of the sleeve tops your next casserole. Cheapest crunch upgrade in the store.
Third-fat cream cheese runs the same price as full-fat but trims cost-per-calorie where it counts. Two 8 ounce bricks were $2.38 on our board.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 3.75 cups dry with water per your usual method.
Cube the chicken breast and cook it in a skillet with a spoonful of the butter over medium-high until it reaches 165 F. Set aside.
In your big pot, melt the rest of the butter, setting aside about 3 tablespoons of it for the topping, and cook the diced onion 4 minutes, then the garlic for 1 more.
Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the chicken broth and heavy cream until smooth and simmering.
Drop in the cream cheese and stir until melted, then add the poppy seeds, salt, and pepper.
Fold in the chicken and the cooked rice, then spread into a greased 9x13 pan.
Crush the butter crackers, toss them with the reserved melted butter, scatter them over the top, and bake at 350 F for 20 to 25 minutes until the topping is golden and the edges bubble.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot before it goes into the pan, subtract the empty pot number from step 1, and divide by 14. After baking, portion by that weight into 14 containers. Each serving comes in at 701 calories and 25 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Hearty dinners for about $1.29 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Poppy seed chicken and rice casserole: 701 calories and 25g protein at about $1.29 a serving. Creamy Southern bake with a buttery cracker topping.
head.keywords: poppy seed chicken casserole, chicken and rice bake, southern casserole recipe, budget chicken dinner, cheap meal prep casserole, creamy chicken rice
steps: Cook cubed chicken in butter to 165 F and set aside.
Cook onion and garlic in butter, whisk in flour, then broth and cream until smooth.
Melt in the cream cheese and add poppy seeds, salt, and pepper.
Fold in chicken and rice, top with buttered cracker crumbs, and bake at 350 F for 20 to 25 minutes.
